The records of the most recent knit

Source: R/state.R
last_knit.Rd

last_knit() returns what weft recorded in the most recent top-level knit in this R session, or NULL before any knit. The records are kept after the knit has ended or failed.

Usage

last_knit()

Value

NULL, or a list with these elements:

  • constructs: a data frame with a row for each construct the scanner found (its file, line, kind, expression, context, chunk, option, arm chosen, whether it was evaluated, and unit_picked: for a construct with a unit key the unit it printed in, as written in its ladder (rule 4.4.23), else NA), or NULL when there was none;

  • failures: a data frame of the failures, one row for each, with the columns kind, file, line, chunk, expr, detail, hint, option and chunk_line;

  • warnings: the checks that were warned about by claim(level = "warn") and the numbers that "printed as zero" (kind "printed as zero"), in the same columns as failures (zero rows when there are none);

  • conditions: a data frame of the warnings and messages that chunks and inline code raised (source, class, text and normalised);

  • ledger: the entries of the ledger the knit recorded, as a data frame of class weft_ledger (the columns of the ledger file, one row for each construct evaluated), for every top-level knit, set up or not;

  • condition_log: the lines of the condition log, as a data frame of class weft_condition_log (from, source, class, normalised and text);

  • output: the output name the ledger files are named by;

  • written: the paths of the ledger and the condition log written, relative to the project root, each NA when nothing was written (the project is not set up, the knit is a rehearsal, or it stopped on its failures);

  • config: the configuration the knit used;

  • sentence_starts: a data frame of the values that start a sentence (file, line, expr and text);

  • dict and dict_local: the project dictionary and the chapter's own, as read_dict() returns them, or NULL when there was none;

  • reads: what the chapter read, as the ledger's header records it (rule 7.2.2): dict and files (named character vectors of hashes, the key or path as the name) and targets (a named list, one named character vector for each targets store). A hash is NA when it could not be taken. NULL for a rehearsal and for a project that is not set up.

Examples

last_knit()
#> NULL
